title: A `@mandate` that fails admission fails every mandate-gated decision closed, and admission refuses a stated `authority.moves []`
summary: Breaking: 2.0.0 admitted a `@mandate` stating `authority.moves []`, and a mandate that failed admission was dropped from the admitted graph, so it silently stopped restricting: a mandate stating `moves [Bogus]` and `excluded-words [task]` let `ia preview task` run, where the same mandate with valid moves refused it (operator ruling 2026-10-12: fail closed for any `@mandate` that fails admission, reject `moves []` in the schema, the refusal names the record, `ia position` and hand edits still work). @inventarch/compliance: schema field validation, which db admission (validateGraphSchema) and the bootstrap validateSchema both run, refuses a stated empty authority.moves on agent-system's `@mandate` with IA-COMP-FIELD-VALUE, an error at that field, each such occurrence on its own, whose message says 'authority.moves' must name at least one kernel move when stated; an absent authority.moves stays valid and restricts no move, and every other empty list stays valid (compliance C05 states this one exception). A workspace 2.0.0 admitted with `moves []` therefore has an admission error now: the machine routes keep their shapes, but over such a workspace the report route lists the finding and the read routes no longer return that mandate. @inventarch/db: every read handle and editor snapshot exposes unadmitted, with the UnadmittedRecord type: each record occurrence of the root view's sources that it does not admit, {identity?, word, band, path, line, endLine, cause}, cause refused for each occurrence refused names, tied for both occurrences of an identity tie, and source for each record of a file refused whole by a language error or a duplicate requirement id, read from db's own parse of that file (with the identity its compile gives, or spec 3.1's for a header the compile refused) and, for a header the parse cannot read, from a line of its captured text that opens with `@<word>`; band is the band of the source's placement; refused, the report, the snapshot and the cache are unchanged, and nothing more is read from disk. @inventarch/runtime: the package root and ./internal/mandate-modes export refusedMandates(handle) with the RefusedMandate type, every authored (band 100) `@mandate` that failed admission, by path then line, each {identity?, path, line, code, message} with the admission finding that refused it; a mandate refused in an installed base (band 90) never counts. While it returns anything, governingMandates, seatedWorkspace and defaultActor throw IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID naming the first (its identity when known, path:line, the admission code and message), workspace-wide whatever the scope token, since a refused record's scope, covers and participant cannot be trusted; RuntimeError gains an optional fourth constructor argument and a frozen where property {path, line, identity?} (the RuntimeWhere type), which that refusal and every mandateAuthorityOf refusal carry; profileRefusal and mandateRefusal keep their own empty-move-list refusal. evaluateMandateGuard's request takes an optional root and its decision an optional where; while an authored mandate fails admission every edit the hook selects is IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE, whoever acts, naming the mandate's path:line, its finding and `ia report` (with --root when the request carries root) rather than `ia validate`, and an admitted mandate whose authority cannot be read still names its governance position. @inventarch/cli: while an authored `@mandate` fails admission, `ia read`, `ia next`, `ia validate`, `ia preview`, `ia author`, `ia capture` (and `ia capture --preview`), `ia compile`, `ia project` and a workspace `ia host <host> --apply` refuse with IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID at exit 1, a where of {path, line, identity} at the first such record (identity null when unknown) and a message naming the record and its admission finding and saying a hand edit corrects it, since `ia preview` and `ia author` cannot target a record admission refused; the next command is `ia report --root <root>`, the version 1 machine route, which no mandate gates and which prints the admission report with the finding (exit 1 for a failing report, nothing on stderr), always with --root: the invocation's, else the root the session opened (forward slashes on win32). An admitted mandate whose authority the runtime cannot read, such as one with a child under authority.moves, still refuses naming its governance position, now with where {path, line, identity}. `ia position`, `ia host <host> --remove --apply` (which still restores editing), `--user`, the Door and MCP reads, the install refresh, `ia-distribution`, `ia inspect` and `ia init` are unchanged and keep running. @inventarch/steward-hook: the `--hook` guard passes the registration's root to evaluateMandateGuard, so a refusal at a refused mandate names `ia report --root <root>`; the main session's refusal still also names `ia host claude --root <root> --remove --apply --yes`; an edit the hook does not select is still not decided and managed-state protection is unchanged; a refusal because the records cannot be read names `ia report --root <root>` instead of `ia validate`; and a registration whose hook is not admitted names `ia report --root <root>` instead of `ia validate --root <root>` while an authored mandate is among what admission refused. @inventarch/workspace-runtime: unchanged source, but agent-profile generation's fallback for a profile that names no mandate reads governingMandates, so while an authored mandate fails admission the rendered agent says the fallback is unavailable and names that mandate. Limits: the fail-closed is workspace-wide, so one broken mandate blocks every gated command and selected edit for every actor until its source is corrected by hand, and no in-tool repair exists; a mandate in a file refused whole is recognised only from db's parse or a line opening with `@mandate`, so a header mangled past that (`@ mandate x`) is not recognised, and a non-header line so spelled in a refused file is read as one, failing closed; position, body(K), the packet renderer and the Door operations render no mandate for a refused record and never refuse; a `@workspace` or a participant `@agent` that fails admission is not covered by this change and can still change which mandates govern or whom they bind; the nine machine routes, MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2 and every `ia scope` form keep their shapes.
